Picked as the best risk-adjusted result of 12 headline setups shown below, so treat it as optimistic. Win rate 44%.

Key takeaways
  • ↑Gold breakout made money on 80% of timeframes tested (profit factor 1.44, 456 trades).
  • ↓Crypto strategies mostly struggled after fees: trend following was profitable on only 31% of 35 coin/timeframe combinations.
  • •Strategies trailed simply holding during strong rallies — e.g. Bitcoin trend +16.9% vs buy & hold +190.2% — but with far smaller drops.
  • ↓High win rate ≠ profit: crypto mean reversion won 46% of trades yet lost money overall (profit factor 0.49).

The honest verdict
  • ↑Buying short, sharp pullbacks in SPY and QQQ while they trade above their 200-day average (RSI(2) and Double-7 rules) wins 71%–77% of trades on unseen data, makes money after fees, survives removing the 20 best trades. The two SPY + QQQ basket versions still pass with every cost ×5 and made money in all 5 unseen windows; they now run as paper accounts.
  • ↓They are not better than simply holding: SPY gained about +806% and QQQ about +1,723% over the same years, versus +100% to +249% for the strategies, which sit in cash about 75–85% of the time (smaller drawdowns, −10% to −15%).
  • ↓Nothing in crypto or gold meets the goal. The old S3 rule still wins 76% of trades but loses money (profit factor 0.83); gold breakout with scale-out wins 78% but its profit rests on a few big trades.
  • •These rule families are well-known published ideas for US stocks, so choosing them was not blind to history; only their settings were picked out-of-sample. 34 combinations were tried, so expect some luck.
Self-learning bot classic report

Self-learning $100 bot

A paper bot that starts with $100 on BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB and XRP, puts most of its balance into one trade at a time (long, or short via a simulated 1× perpetual), and learns which of 24 strategy settings work from its own closed trades after fees. If the balance falls below $10 (or 10% of its peak) it is “busted” and restarts with a fresh $100, keeping what it learned. Position size shrinks as the balance grows: 80% of the balance at $100, 70% at $200, 50% at $500, 30% at $1,000 and 17.5% from $5,000 (never below 15%). Fees 0.10% per side plus slippage; shorts pay funding.

The honest verdict
  • ↓Nothing tested makes money after costs. The team lost −$2,811 (−28.1%) on unseen data — better than the three old strategies combined, but still a clear loss.

  • ↓Every bot loses on its own, and all 4 unseen windows lost. Of 432 captain settings tried, 4 were profitable on both training and unseen data — each with only a handful of trades, which is luck, not an edge.
  • •The live account runs anyway so you can watch the costs at work trade by trade.

Methodology & data sources
Methodology & data sources

How strategies are tested

Walk-forward testing: settings are chosen on an earlier stretch of data, then the strategy is scored on the following stretch it has never seen, repeated across 4 windows (3 where history is short) and stitched together. Settings are chosen by average result per trade, never by win rate. Every trade enters at the next candle's open; if a stop and a target are hit in the same candle, the stop is assumed.

Costs

  • Crypto: 0.10% fee per side plus 2–5 basis points slippage per side (by timeframe).
  • Gold: 0.005% per side (spread + commission) plus 1–1.5 bp slippage per side and 0.005% per day financing; position size may reach 5× the account (risk still capped at 1% per trade).

Position sizing & risk rules

Quarter-Kelly sizing from past closed trades, capped at 1% of the account at risk per trade; new trades pause after a 3% daily loss or a 20% drop from the peak.

Data

  • Crypto: Binance public market data (no account), 7 coins, 5-minute to daily candles.
  • Gold: COMEX gold futures (Yahoo symbol GC=F, unadjusted continuous contract, so contract rolls/glitches can cause jumps). 5- and 15-minute history is only ~60 days. Cross-checked against PAXG (a gold-backed token on Binance).
  • Portfolio: daily BTC-USD, QQQ (Nasdaq-100) and GLD (gold) via Yahoo Finance.
  • Micro-trades: PAXG/USDT 1-minute bars (incl. taker buy volume for order flow) and individual public trades from Binance, polled every 2 seconds (streaming isn't available from the research box). Cross-checked against COMEX gold futures 1-minute data (GC=F, 7,885 shared minutes): correlation 0.85 minute-by-minute and 0.96 over 5 minutes; PAXG traded a median 0.48% below the futures price.

Micro-trade costs (MT5 XAUUSD raw-spread CFD account)

  • PAXG and COMEX futures prices are used only for timing; every trade is costed as if placed on an MT5 XAUUSD account (1 lot = 100 oz, minimum 0.01 lot, 1:100 leverage).
  • Spread by London session: Asia $0.25/oz, London $0.14, London–New York overlap $0.12, New York $0.16, rollover 21:00–23:00 $0.45 — widened when the recent market is more volatile than usual (up to 4×).
  • Commission $7 per lot round turn; slippage $0.03/oz on market orders and $0.08/oz on stops; overnight swap charged past 22:00 London (long −$45, short +$10 per lot per night, triple on Wednesdays). The captain is flat by 21:55 London, so it normally pays no swap.
  • Risk caps: 0.5% of the account at risk per captain trade, at most 3 new trades a minute, trading stops for the day after a 2% loss. If a stop and a target are both hit within the same minute, the stop is assumed.

Range of outcomes

2,000 bootstrap resamples of each setup's tested trades; it shows luck, not regime changes, outages or liquidity.

Things to keep in mind

  • Headline setups are the best of many tested combinations, so their results are optimistic.
  • Gold breakout's gains came mostly from long trades during a strong gold bull market.
  • Paper accounts started on 9 Oct 2026 and have too few trades to judge.
  • Simulated results only. Not financial advice. Past and backtested performance does not predict future results.
